headline: Cardinals' five-run 17th sinks Phillies in marathon
recap: Three singles, two walks and two sacrifice flies produced five runs for St. Louis in the top of the 17th inning, breaking a 2-2 tie that had held since the third. Ted Simmons, Keith Hernandez, Bake McBride, Ken Reitz and Luis Melendez each came around to score during the rally, which chased Jesus Hernaiz and Eddie Watt from the game before Tom Underwood recorded the final two outs of the frame. Mike Schmidt led off the bottom of the 17th with a triple, his seventh of the season, and scored on a single by Willie Montanez, but the Phillies got no closer, falling 7-3.
Starters Jim Lonborg of the Phillies and Lynn McGlothen of the Cardinals matched each other for eight innings, each allowing seven hits, five walks and two runs before leaving with the score tied.

St. Louis reliever Ray Bare threw four hitless, walk-free innings to bridge the middle of the game and picked up the win. The Phillies used eight pitchers in all, with Hernaiz failing to record an out in the decisive 17th.
